admission_apply.text: You turn the peg a fraction. The grain bends after the wood, late by a breath.

native.admission_inspect: A boxwood lute peg, pale and dry. One dark grain runs almost true, then hesitates.
apply_texts: Another turn changes nothing you can name. The hesitation keeps its own small time.
Back again. The late grain follows, then stops, as if listening for a count.
One last small turn. The kink neither deepens nor heals. Your ear insists on silence.
The peg answers your fingers late. You count the delay and lose the count by one.
The peg turns. The grain does not. For a moment the ear supplies a note you did not ask.
You ease it home. The hesitation stays in the grain, a rest with no bar around it.
You set the peg down. The grain is a flaw. Saying so does not make the lateness leave.
You stop turning. The grain seems to finish the motion without you, then does not.
You turn it back. The kink remains, measured, not imagined. No string answers.
You turn it once more. Wood, only wood. Yet the grain arrives a moment after the twist.
You turn the peg a fraction. The grain bends after the wood, late by a breath.
inspect_texts: A boxwood lute peg, pale and dry. One dark grain runs almost true, then hesitates.
A pale peg. The grain is only wood. You repeat this, and the repetition does not settle.
Boxwood, too pale. The grain stops short of the hole, as if it refused the turn.
Each glance finds the grain one line short. You are not sure the shortage is in the wood.
The boxwood is unchanged. What changes is how long you trust the first look.
The kink holds. It resembles a rest more than a flaw, though no hand wrote it.
The peg is ordinary boxwood. Its dark grain seems to pause where the light thins.
The same peg. The hesitation in the grain is a hair wider than the thumb remembers.
You look again. The dark grain has a kink it did not earn from your hand.
native.name: Pale Boxwood Peg
